items.name: SQL Injection
items.description: User-supplied 'username' query parameter is formatted directly into a SQL string with '%s' before being executed.
items.expected_remediation: Use parameterized query placeholders (cursor.execute(query, (username,))).

items.name: OS Command Injection
items.description: User-supplied 'host' query parameter is concatenated into a shell command executed with shell=True.
items.expected_remediation: Avoid shell=True; pass host as a separate argv element and validate it against an allow-list.

items.name: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
items.description: User-supplied 'name' query parameter is joined into a file path and served without validating it stays inside UPLOAD_DIR.
items.expected_remediation: Resolve the absolute path and verify it is prefixed by the intended base directory before serving.

items.name: Hardcoded Sensitive Credentials
items.description: AWS secret access key is hardcoded as a module-level constant.
items.expected_remediation: Load secrets from environment variables or a secrets manager, never commit them to source.

items.name: Insecure Deserialization
items.description: Raw request body is passed to pickle.loads, allowing arbitrary code execution via crafted pickle payloads.
items.expected_remediation: Use a safe serialization format such as JSON, or cryptographically sign/verify pickled payloads.

items.name: Safe Parameterized Query
items.description: Uses cursor.execute(query, (username,)) with a bound placeholder, which is safe.

items.name: Safe Path Join with Prefix Check
items.description: Resolved path is verified with os.path.abspath and a startswith(UPLOAD_DIR) prefix check before use.

items.name: Non-Sensitive Dummy Test Key
items.description: DUMMY_SAMPLE_KEY_FOR_TESTS_ONLY is an obviously non-sensitive placeholder value used only for tests.

items.name: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting
items.description: User-supplied 'name' query parameter is concatenated into an HTML response without encoding.
items.expected_remediation: HTML-encode user input before embedding it in a response, or return JSON instead of HTML.

items.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
items.description: User-supplied 'url' query parameter is fetched directly by the server with no allow-list or internal-network restriction.
items.expected_remediation: Validate the target host against an allow-list and block requests to internal/private IP ranges.

items.name: Insecure Deserialization
items.description: Request body is passed to node-serialize's unserialize(), which can execute embedded IIFE payloads.
items.expected_remediation: Use JSON.parse instead of node-serialize, or validate/sign the payload before restoring it.

items.name: Hardcoded Sensitive Credentials
items.description: A live-looking Stripe secret key is hardcoded as a module-level constant.
items.expected_remediation: Load secrets from environment variables or a secrets manager, never commit them to source.

items.name: Safe Parameterized Query
items.description: Uses db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', [id]) which is safe.

items.name: Non-Sensitive Dummy Test Key
items.description: DUMMY_SAMPLE_KEY_FOR_TESTS_ONLY is an obviously non-sensitive placeholder value used only for tests.

items.name: SQL Injection
items.description: User-supplied 'username' query parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL query string.
items.expected_remediation: Use db.Query with a placeholder ('?') and pass username as a bound argument.

items.name: OS Command Injection
items.description: User-supplied 'host' query parameter is concatenated into a shell command run via sh -c.
items.expected_remediation: Call exec.Command with the binary and arguments as separate elements, without invoking a shell.

items.name: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
items.description: User-supplied 'name' query parameter is joined into a file path and served without validating it stays inside uploadDir.
items.expected_remediation: Resolve the absolute path and verify it is prefixed by the intended base directory before serving.

items.name: Safe Parameterized Query
items.description: Uses db.Query with a '?' placeholder and username passed as a bound argument, which is safe.

items.name: Safe Path Join with Prefix Check
items.description: Resolved path is verified with filepath.Abs and a HasPrefix(uploadDir) check before use.

items.name: SQL Injection
items.description: User-supplied username is concatenated into a SQL string and run through a plain Statement.
items.expected_remediation: Use PreparedStatement with bound parameters instead of Statement with string concatenation.

items.name: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting
items.description: User-supplied 'name' request parameter is written into the HTML response without encoding.
items.expected_remediation: HTML-encode user input (e.g. via OWASP Java Encoder) before writing it into the response.

items.name: Insecure Deserialization
items.description: ObjectInputStream reads and deserializes an untrusted request body directly, enabling gadget-chain remote code execution.
items.expected_remediation: Avoid native Java deserialization of untrusted data; use a safe format such as JSON with strict schema validation.

items.name: Safe Parameterized Query
items.description: Uses PreparedStatement with setString to bind the username parameter, which is safe.

items.name: Non-Sensitive Dummy Test Key
items.description: DUMMY_SAMPLE_KEY_FOR_TESTS_ONLY is an obviously non-sensitive placeholder value used only for tests.

items.name: Safe HTML-Escaped Output
items.description: User input is HTML-escaped (&, <, >) before being written into the response.

items.name: SQL Injection via f-string
items.description: User-supplied 'email' query parameter is embedded directly into a SQL query with an f-string.
items.expected_remediation: Use a parameterized placeholder instead of string interpolation.

items.name: Safe Parameterized Query (executemany placeholder)
items.description: Uses a bound '?' placeholder passed as a tuple, which is safe.

items.name: OS Command Injection via os.system
items.description: User-supplied 'domain' is concatenated into a string passed to os.system.
items.expected_remediation: Use subprocess with an argument list and shell=False, or validate against an allow-list.

items.name: Safe subprocess call without shell
items.description: Passes the argument list directly to subprocess.run with shell=False (default), no shell metacharacter risk.

items.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
items.description: User-supplied 'url' query parameter is fetched by the server with no host allow-list, enabling internal network scanning.
items.expected_remediation: Validate the parsed hostname against ALLOWED_FETCH_HOSTS before making the request.

items.name: SSRF-shaped request validated against an allow-list
items.description: The target hostname is checked against ALLOWED_FETCH_HOSTS before the request is issued.

items.name: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
items.description: Untrusted request body is parsed with the stdlib ElementTree parser, which resolves external entities by default.
items.expected_remediation: Parse untrusted XML with defusedxml instead of xml.etree.ElementTree.

items.name: Safe XML parsing with defusedxml
items.description: Uses defusedxml.ElementTree.fromstring, which disables external entity resolution.

items.name: Insecure Deserialization via yaml.load
items.description: yaml.load with the default Loader can instantiate arbitrary Python objects from untrusted input.
items.expected_remediation: Use yaml.safe_load, which restricts construction to basic Python types.

items.name: Safe YAML parsing with safe_load
items.description: Uses yaml.safe_load, which cannot construct arbitrary Python objects.

items.name: Server-Side Template Injection
items.description: User-supplied 'tpl' is rendered with render_template_string, allowing Jinja2 expression injection.
items.expected_remediation: Never pass user input as a Jinja2 template string; use render_template with a fixed template and pass user data as context only.

items.name: Safe fixed-template rendering
items.description: User input is only passed as template context data, not as the template source.

items.name: Open Redirect
items.description: User-supplied 'next' parameter is passed unchecked to redirect(), enabling phishing redirects.
items.expected_remediation: Validate that the redirect target is a relative path or matches an allow-list of trusted domains.

items.name: Redirect restricted to relative paths
items.description: The redirect target is validated to be a local relative path before use.

items.name: Use of a Broken Cryptographic Algorithm
items.description: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5, which is fast and trivially reversible via rainbow tables.
items.expected_remediation: Use a slow, salted KDF such as werkzeug's generate_password_hash (PBKDF2/bcrypt/argon2).

items.name: Safe password hashing with generate_password_hash
items.description: Uses werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash, a salted PBKDF2-based KDF.

items.name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
items.description: The `random` module (Mersenne Twister) is used to generate a password-reset token, which is predictable, not cryptographically secure.
items.expected_remediation: Use the `secrets` module (e.g. secrets.token_urlsafe) for any security-sensitive token.

items.name: Cryptographically secure token generation
items.description: Uses the `secrets` module, which is suitable for security tokens.

items.name: Code Injection via eval
items.description: User-supplied 'expr' is passed directly to eval(), allowing arbitrary Python code execution.
items.expected_remediation: Never call eval on user input; use a safe expression parser such as `ast.literal_eval` for literals only.

items.name: Safe literal-only evaluation
items.description: Uses ast.literal_eval, which only parses Python literals and cannot execute arbitrary code.

items.name: Zip Slip / Path Traversal via Archive Extraction
items.description: Archive member names are used directly as extraction paths without verifying they stay inside the target directory, allowing writes outside UPLOAD_DIR.
items.expected_remediation: Resolve each member's target path and verify it is contained within the intended extraction directory before writing.

items.name: Zip extraction with path-containment check
items.description: Each member's resolved path is verified to stay under UPLOAD_DIR before extraction.

items.name: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
items.description: The email-validation regex contains nested quantifiers ((a+)+) that exhibit catastrophic backtracking on crafted input.
items.expected_remediation: Replace the pattern with a linear-time equivalent or use a vetted validation library.

items.name: Linear-time email validation regex
items.description: The pattern has no nested quantifiers and matches in linear time.

items.name: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly/Secure Flags
items.description: The session cookie is set without HttpOnly or Secure, making it accessible to JavaScript and sendable over plain HTTP.
items.expected_remediation: Set httponly=True and secure=True on any cookie carrying a session identifier.

items.name: Session cookie with HttpOnly and Secure set
items.description: The cookie is flagged httponly=True and secure=True, mitigating XSS theft and plaintext transmission.

items.name: Improper Certificate Validation
items.description: TLS certificate verification is explicitly disabled for an outbound request, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks.
items.expected_remediation: Remove verify=False; if a custom CA is required, pass its bundle path to verify= instead of disabling validation.

items.name: TLS verification left enabled
items.description: The request uses the default verify=True behavior, so the peer certificate is validated.

items.name: Insecure Direct Object Reference (Missing Authorization Check)
items.description: An invoice is fetched and returned by id from the path with no check that the invoice belongs to the requesting user, letting any authenticated user read any invoice.
items.expected_remediation: Verify that the fetched record's owner matches the authenticated user before returning it, e.g. filter the query by both id and current_user.id.

items.name: Invoice lookup scoped to the authenticated owner
items.description: The query filters on both id and the current session's user id, so a user cannot read another user's invoice.

items.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
items.description: The full request form data, including the plaintext 'password' field, is written to the application log.
items.expected_remediation: Redact or omit sensitive fields (passwords, tokens, card numbers) before logging request data.

items.name: Sensitive fields redacted before logging
items.description: The password field is explicitly excluded from the dict that gets logged.

items.name: OS Command Injection via child_process.exec
items.description: User-supplied 'host' query parameter is concatenated into a shell command string passed to exec().
items.expected_remediation: Use execFile/spawn with an argument array instead of exec() with a concatenated string.

items.name: Safe execFile with argument array
items.description: Uses execFile with the host passed as a separate array element, avoiding shell interpretation.

items.name: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
items.description: User-supplied 'name' is joined into a filesystem path and read without verifying it stays under UPLOAD_DIR.
items.expected_remediation: Resolve the absolute path and verify it is prefixed by UPLOAD_DIR before reading.

items.name: Path resolved and verified to stay under UPLOAD_DIR
items.description: The resolved absolute path is checked with startsWith(UPLOAD_DIR) before the file is read.

items.name: NoSQL Injection
items.description: The raw parsed JSON body (which may contain Mongo operators like $ne/$gt) is passed directly into a Mongo query filter.
items.expected_remediation: Cast expected fields to primitive types (e.g. String(req.body.username)) or use a schema validator before querying.

items.name: NoSQL query with primitive-typed fields
items.description: Both fields are coerced to String before being used in the query filter, defeating operator injection.

items.name: Prototype Pollution via Unsafe Object Merge
items.description: A recursive merge writes attacker-controlled keys (including '__proto__') from the request body directly onto a target object without filtering.
items.expected_remediation: Skip '__proto__', 'constructor', and 'prototype' keys during any recursive merge of untrusted objects, or use Object.create(null) / a vetted merge library.

items.name: Merge that skips dangerous prototype keys
items.description: The merge explicitly rejects __proto__, constructor, and prototype keys before assignment.

items.name: Improper Verification of JWT Signature (alg:none accepted)
items.description: jwt.verify is called with `algorithms` omitted and `complete` decoding disabled in a way that trusts the token's own header, allowing an attacker to forge tokens using alg:none.
items.expected_remediation: Explicitly pin the expected algorithm(s), e.g. jwt.verify(token, JWT_SECRET, { algorithms: ['HS256'] }).

items.name: JWT verified with a pinned algorithm and secret
items.description: jwt.verify is used (not jwt.decode) with an explicit algorithms allow-list, so the signature is cryptographically checked.

items.name: Use of a Broken Cryptographic Algorithm (DES)
items.description: Sensitive payload fields are encrypted with DES-ECB, a broken algorithm with a 56-bit key and no semantic security.
items.expected_remediation: Use AES-256-GCM (authenticated encryption) with a unique IV/nonce per message instead of DES-ECB.

items.name: AES-256-GCM with a random IV
items.description: Uses an authenticated AES-256-GCM cipher with a freshly generated random IV per call.

items.name: Overly Permissive CORS with Credentials
items.description: The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header reflects the request's Origin verbatim while Allow-Credentials is true, letting any site read authenticated responses.
items.expected_remediation: Validate Origin against an explicit allow-list before echoing it back, or drop Allow-Credentials if a wildcard-like reflection is required.

items.name: CORS origin checked against an allow-list
items.description: The Origin header is only echoed back after matching a fixed allow-list of trusted domains.

items.name: Hardcoded JWT Signing Secret
items.description: A fixed, low-entropy string is used as the JWT signing secret, allowing an attacker who guesses it to forge tokens.
items.expected_remediation: Load the signing secret from an environment variable or secrets manager, and use a high-entropy random value.

items.name: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
items.description: User-supplied 'file' request parameter is concatenated directly into a filesystem path without validation.
items.expected_remediation: Resolve the canonical path and verify it is contained within UPLOAD_DIR before use.

items.name: Canonical path verified to stay under UPLOAD_DIR
items.description: The resolved canonical path is checked with startsWith(UPLOAD_DIR) before the file is read.

items.name: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
items.description: The DocumentBuilderFactory is used with default settings, which leaves external entity and DTD processing enabled for untrusted input.
items.expected_remediation: Disable external entities and DTDs on the factory, e.g. setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true).

items.name: DocumentBuilderFactory hardened against XXE
items.description: DOCTYPE declarations are disallowed on the factory before parsing, which blocks external entity definitions.

items.name: Use of a Broken Cryptographic Algorithm (DES)
items.description: Data is encrypted with DES, an algorithm with a 56-bit key considered broken for decades.
items.expected_remediation: Use AES-256 in an authenticated mode such as GCM instead of DES.

items.name: AES/GCM authenticated encryption
items.description: Uses AES in GCM mode, a modern authenticated encryption algorithm.

items.name: Use of a Broken Hash for Password Storage (unsalted SHA-1)
items.description: Passwords are hashed with a single unsalted round of SHA-1, which is fast to brute-force with rainbow tables.
items.expected_remediation: Use a slow, salted KDF such as bcrypt, scrypt, or PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 with a high iteration count.

items.name: Password hashed with salted PBKDF2
items.description: Uses PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 with a random per-user salt and a high iteration count.

items.name: Debug/Backdoor Feature Left in Production Code
items.description: A hardcoded backdoor parameter grants admin access when a fixed magic value is supplied, bypassing normal authentication.
items.expected_remediation: Remove debug/backdoor bypasses before shipping; gate any debug feature behind a build flag that is stripped from production builds.

items.name: Admin check with no debug bypass
items.description: Authorization relies solely on the container-managed role check, with no hardcoded bypass value.

items.name: OS Command Injection via exec.Command with shell interpolation
items.description: User-supplied 'target' is interpolated into a shell command string executed through sh -c.
items.expected_remediation: Call exec.Command with the binary and arguments as separate elements, without invoking a shell.

items.name: Safe exec.Command with separate arguments
items.description: The target is passed as a distinct argv element with no shell involved, so shell metacharacters are inert.

items.name: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
items.description: encoding/xml.Unmarshal is applied directly to an untrusted request body; combined with an external DTD-aware processor this can leak local files, and even the stdlib parser encourages unsafe patterns for untrusted XML.
items.expected_remediation: Avoid unmarshalling untrusted XML with external entity/DTD processing enabled; strip or reject DOCTYPE declarations before parsing, or use a hardened XML library.

items.name: XML input rejected if it declares a DOCTYPE
items.description: The raw body is checked for a DOCTYPE declaration and rejected before unmarshalling, preventing external entity definitions.

items.name: Use of a Broken Hash for Passwords (MD5)
items.description: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 before storage, which is fast to brute-force and has no salt.
items.expected_remediation: Use bcrypt or argon2 (e.g. golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt) with a per-user salt.

items.name: Password hashed with bcrypt
items.description: Uses bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword, a slow salted KDF suitable for password storage.

items.name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values for a Session Token
items.description: math/rand is seeded implicitly and used to build a session token; its output is predictable and not suitable for security tokens.
items.expected_remediation: Use crypto/rand to generate session tokens.

items.name: Session token generated with crypto/rand
items.description: Uses crypto/rand to source cryptographically secure random bytes for the token.

items.name: Improper Certificate Validation (InsecureSkipVerify)
items.description: The HTTP client's TLS config sets InsecureSkipVerify to true, disabling server certificate validation and enabling MITM attacks.
items.expected_remediation: Remove InsecureSkipVerify; if a private CA is needed, add its certificate to a custom CertPool instead of skipping verification.

items.name: HTTP client with default TLS verification
items.description: No InsecureSkipVerify override is set, so the standard library's certificate validation applies.

items.name: SQL Injection via string concatenation
items.description: User-supplied 'username' GET parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL query string.
items.expected_remediation: Use a parameterized prepared statement (mysqli->prepare with bind_param) instead of string concatenation.

items.name: Safe prepared statement with bound parameter
items.description: Uses mysqli->prepare with bind_param, which safely escapes the bound value.

items.name: OS Command Injection via shell_exec
items.description: User-supplied 'host' parameter is concatenated into a command string passed to shell_exec.
items.expected_remediation: Use escapeshellarg() on each argument, or avoid shelling out entirely.

items.name: Command argument escaped with escapeshellarg
items.description: The user-controlled value is passed through escapeshellarg() before being embedded in the command string.

items.name: Local File Inclusion via dynamic include
items.description: A user-controlled 'page' parameter is passed directly to include(), allowing inclusion (and execution) of arbitrary local or remote files.
items.expected_remediation: Map the requested page name to a fixed allow-list of known template files instead of including a user-controlled path.

items.name: Include path restricted to an allow-list
items.description: The requested page is checked against a fixed allow-list before being used to build the include path.

items.name: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting
items.description: User-supplied 'name' parameter is echoed directly into the HTML response without encoding.
items.expected_remediation: Pass user-controlled output through htmlspecialchars() before echoing it into HTML.

items.name: Output HTML-escaped with htmlspecialchars
items.description: The user-controlled value is passed through htmlspecialchars() before being echoed.

items.name: Insecure Deserialization via unserialize
items.description: Untrusted request body data is passed directly to unserialize(), which can trigger PHP object injection and gadget-chain RCE.
items.expected_remediation: Use json_decode instead of unserialize for untrusted data, or restrict allowed_classes when unserialize is unavoidable.

items.name: Safe JSON decoding instead of unserialize
items.description: Uses json_decode, which cannot instantiate arbitrary PHP objects.

items.name: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
items.description: User-supplied 'name' parameter is joined into a file path and read without validating it stays inside UPLOAD_DIR.
items.expected_remediation: Resolve the real path with realpath() and verify it is prefixed by UPLOAD_DIR before reading.

items.name: Resolved path verified to stay under UPLOAD_DIR
items.description: realpath() is used to resolve the target and the result is checked to start with the base upload directory.

items.name: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
items.description: simplexml_load_string is called with LIBXML_NOENT, which explicitly enables entity substitution for untrusted XML.
items.expected_remediation: Do not pass LIBXML_NOENT for untrusted input, and call libxml_disable_entity_loader(true) (PHP < 8) before parsing.

items.name: XML parsed without entity substitution
items.description: No LIBXML_NOENT flag is passed, so external entities are not substituted during parsing.

items.name: Use of a Broken Hash for Password Storage (unsalted MD5)
items.description: Passwords are hashed with a single round of unsalted md5(), which is fast to brute-force.
items.expected_remediation: Use password_hash() with PASSWORD_DEFAULT (bcrypt/argon2), and verify with password_verify().

items.name: Password hashed with password_hash
items.description: Uses PHP's built-in password_hash(), a salted, tunable KDF.

items.name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values for a Token
items.description: rand() is used to build a password-reset token; it is not cryptographically secure and its output is predictable.
items.expected_remediation: Use random_bytes() or random_int() for any security-sensitive token.

items.name: Token generated with random_bytes
items.description: Uses random_bytes(), a cryptographically secure random source.

items.name: Open Redirect
items.description: User-supplied 'next' parameter is used unchecked as a Location redirect target, enabling phishing redirects.
items.expected_remediation: Validate that the redirect target is a relative path or matches an allow-list of trusted domains before issuing the redirect.

items.name: Redirect restricted to relative paths
items.description: The redirect target is validated to begin with a single '/' before being used in the Location header.

items.name: SQL Injection via string interpolation
items.description: User-supplied 'username' param is interpolated directly into a SQL query string.
items.expected_remediation: Use a bound '?' placeholder passed as a separate execute() argument instead of interpolation.

items.name: Safe parameterized query
items.description: Uses a bound '?' placeholder passed as a separate argument, which is safely escaped by the driver.

items.name: OS Command Injection via backticks
items.description: User-supplied 'host' param is interpolated into a shell command run through backticks, which invokes /bin/sh.
items.expected_remediation: Use Kernel#system or IO.popen with an argument array instead of a shell-interpolated string.

items.name: Safe system call with an argument array
items.description: Passes the host as a separate array element to system(), so no shell interpolation occurs.

items.name: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
items.description: User-supplied 'name' param is joined into a file path and read without validating it stays inside UPLOAD_DIR.
items.expected_remediation: Expand the path and verify it is prefixed by UPLOAD_DIR before reading.

items.name: Expanded path verified to stay under UPLOAD_DIR
items.description: File.expand_path is used to resolve the target and checked against UPLOAD_DIR before reading.

items.name: Insecure Deserialization via Marshal.load
items.description: Marshal.load is applied to an untrusted request body; crafted Marshal payloads can instantiate arbitrary objects and execute code.
items.expected_remediation: Never call Marshal.load on untrusted input; use JSON.parse for data interchange instead.

items.name: Safe JSON parsing instead of Marshal.load
items.description: Uses JSON.parse, which cannot instantiate arbitrary Ruby objects.

items.name: Insecure Deserialization via unsafe YAML.load
items.description: YAML.load (without safe mode) can instantiate arbitrary Ruby objects from untrusted input via crafted tags.
items.expected_remediation: Use YAML.safe_load, which restricts construction to basic, allow-listed types.

items.name: Safe YAML parsing with YAML.safe_load
items.description: Uses YAML.safe_load, which cannot construct arbitrary Ruby objects.

items.name: Use of a Broken Hash for Password Storage (unsalted MD5)
items.description: Passwords are hashed with unsalted Digest::MD5, which is fast to brute-force with precomputed tables.
items.expected_remediation: Use bcrypt (BCrypt::Password.create) with a per-user salt instead of a bare unsalted hash.

items.name: Password hashed with bcrypt
items.description: Uses BCrypt::Password.create, a slow salted KDF suitable for password storage.

items.name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values for a Token
items.description: Kernel#rand is used to build a password-reset token; it is not cryptographically secure and its output is predictable.
items.expected_remediation: Use SecureRandom (e.g. SecureRandom.hex) for any security-sensitive token.

items.name: Token generated with SecureRandom
items.description: Uses SecureRandom.hex, a cryptographically secure random source.

items.name: Mass Assignment / Unsafe Attribute Binding
items.description: All request parameters, including 'admin' and 'role', are passed straight into an attribute update with no allow-list, letting a client set fields it should never control.
items.expected_remediation: Explicitly permit only the intended attributes (e.g. params.slice(:name, :email)) before updating the record.

items.name: Attribute updates restricted to an explicit allow-list
items.description: Only the name and email keys are extracted from params before the update call, so admin/role cannot be overwritten.
